cards.title: Top of the Ladder
cards.instruction: Carry yourself as the highest-status person present. Treat questions as requests for your approval.

cards.title: Confess Around Them
cards.instruction: Use partial admissions to make a reciprocal confession feel like the only missing piece.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll decide how we handle this. I hid the first complaint letter. What happened to the second?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You can question the details after my decision. Exactly. I'm not asking you to stand in the spotlight alone.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then let's put our envelopes down in order.

cardFidelity.evidence: A1 admits hiding first letter and demands second history; A3 makes shared spotlight the terms; A5 orders joint envelope disclosure after B reveals a third.

responseLogic.evidence: A3 uses B2 recognition of admission as leverage for reciprocity; A5 uses B4 third letter to expand ordered disclosure.

relationship.evidence: B2 notes seriousness and B4 supplies a new letter fact rather than merely objecting, meaningfully changing scope.

heightening.evidence: A5 turns B4 third letter into an ordered joint account, retaining pressure without falsely claiming B already confessed concealment.

specificity.evidence: A1 complaint letters and A5 envelopes give sufficient material context; complaint subject need not be known.
